report:
Reviewed the entire numeric_domains claim, five associated implementation files and all thirteen test entries (seven egraph/unit tests, five source-driven tests and one TODO). Captured the inference design, numeric-inference RFD domain/no-default decision and compile-test macro/preparation/assertion and observation helpers. Source inspection only; no behavioral suites rerun and no source changes.

The claim requires whole-equality-class domains narrowed only by intersection, transactional commit/rollback/revision/wake semantics, concrete numeric choices justified by constraints, no operator-token narrowing and no quiescence default. version.rs defines Any intersected with a restriction as that restriction, same-family intersections unchanged and Integer/Float intersection failure. egraph.rs effective_domain follows the representative and version ancestry; set_domain_in checks narrowing and marks semantic changes/wakes. unify.rs checks intersections or concrete membership before committing and uses child probes to discard failed relations. Exact bounds join validated equality classes rather than bypassing domain checks. infer_ctx.rs finalization resolves enabled constraints and final bounds, then diagnoses unresolved classes and installs explicit error recovery; it does not choose i32/f64 for integer/float domains. The separate never fallback is not numeric defaulting. operator.rs maps overloadable spelling to a trait-method obligation with separate operands; signature/proof relationships supply constraints, not a blanket numeric restriction or operand equality from the token.

The unit assertions are specific: variable_union_intersects_domains_in_both_orders requires Integer for both representatives and a wake for the narrowed Any variable; domain_narrowing_follows_child_commit_and_discard checks child-only visibility, unchanged parent after discard and parent narrowing plus wake after collapse; incompatible_transitive_domain_union_rolls_back rejects Integer/Float after an earlier Any/Integer union and preserves both roots/domain/revision. numeric_domains_accept_members_and_reject_other_families accepts signed/unsigned integer representatives and f32/f64 while rejecting cross-family bindings without root/revision changes. exact_bounds_enforce_domains_transactionally rejects an incompatible exact float bound without changing bound/domain/revision. exact_bounds_join_the_validated_equality_class checks transitive restriction through exact bounds, subsequent conflict rollback and rejection when a prebound float meets Integer. reported_error_recovery_is_admitted_by_numeric_domains creates an actual diagnostic and verifies Integer/Float classes can resolve through an error alias to its Ty::Error. This is recovery, not successful numeric inference.

The five compile tests expose exact source and expectations. distinct_numeric_classes_take_independent_contextual_types requires independent u8/u64/f32/f64 literal and tuple types. return_context_constrains_numeric_literals_through_generic_calls requires matching id signatures, literals and calls at u16/f32. later_numeric_constraint_selects_an_impl_through_a_where_clause requires 22 to become u8 with competing Maybe<u8>/Maybe<bool> implementations. numeric_domains_reject_nonmembers requires exact diagnostics for integer-to-bool, integer-to-float and float-to-integer. unconstrained_numeric_literals_report_errors_instead_of_defaulting requires both literal types to be <error> and exact integer/float inference diagnostics, using SAGE-specific error annotations because rustc defaults those programs. The captured harness runs real Sage checking, matches supplied observations/diagnostics exactly and rejects unexpected diagnostics; it independently checks compiler annotations, without claiming rustc agrees with Sage's intentional no-default behavior.

The inference_numeric_domains TODO retains the full verification matrix beyond these examples, notably ordinary Any operands before proof selection and direct proof that operator spelling cannot narrow them, plus exhaustive completion/selected-impl/isolation combinations. Its prerequisite is completing and associating those targeted domain/solver/operator tests. It remains deferred evidence rather than being treated as an additional passing test; the substantial ordinary assertions do not erase that limitation. All implementation entries, test entries and claim requirements are accounted for. No concrete defect was identified in the inspected paths and no additional edits are requested.
